title: Fifth Update on Whole-of-Government Responses to COVID-19
what_it_is: Fifth Update on Whole-of-Government Responses to COVID-19

sections.label: Nightlife suspension and contact rings
sections.summary: Contacts were identified and tested for COVID-19, and pivoted nightlife establishments had operations suspended from 16 to 30 July.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: We identified rings of contacts and tested them for COVID-19.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: We ordered a two-week suspension of operations in all pivoted nightlife establishments from 16 July till 30 July.

sections.label: MTF decision on opening up
sections.summary: The MTF concluded the cluster should not significantly change opening plans, citing tracing, testing and vaccination rate approaching 50%.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: The MTF deliberated on the matter, took in advice from MOH experts and came to the conclusion that, given our extensive tracing and testing efforts and our population vaccination rate for two doses was approaching 50% at that time, on balance, we felt that the cluster ought not significantly change our plans to open up.

sections.label: KTV cluster case count
sections.summary: As of 25 July 2021, the KTV cluster had a total of 237 infected persons.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: As of 25 July 2021, that means end of yesterday, the KTV cluster has a total of 237 infected persons.

sections.label: Positive results among tested
sections.summary: Of the 1,548 tested, 43 were found to be COVID-19 positive.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Of the 1,548 tested, 43 were found to be COVID-19 positive.

sections.label: Return to Heightened Alert
sections.summary: The MTF decided to pre-emptively dial back to Phase Two (Heightened Alert) because infections could cause severe illness or deaths among seniors.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: These infections could potentially result in more cases of severe illnesses or even deaths among our vulnerable senior population.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Hence, the MTF decided to pre-emptively dial back to Phase Two (Heightened Alert).

sections.label: Jurong Fishery Port case count
sections.summary: As of 25 July 2021, the Jurong Fishery Port had a total of 792 cases.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: As of 25 July 2021, the Jurong Fishery Port has a total of 792 cases.

sections.label: Population vaccination rate progress
sections.summary: As of 25 July 2021, 54% of the population had two mRNA vaccine doses, rising about one percentage point daily, so almost 70% will by National Day.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: As of end of yesterday, 25 July 2021, 54% of our population has received two doses of the mRNA vaccine.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: And our population vaccination rate is going up by about one percentage point a day.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: So, by National Day, almost 70% will have received two doses.

sections.label: Seniors vaccinated under programme
sections.summary: As of 23 July, 734 seniors had received vaccinations under that programme.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: As of 23 July, 734 seniors had received vaccinations under that programme.

sections.label: Seniors first dose coverage
sections.summary: 77% of seniors aged 70 and above have now received their first doses.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: As a result of all these efforts, 77% of our seniors 70 years and above have now received their first doses.

sections.label: Severe illness patients vaccination status
sections.summary: All patients with severe illnesses are currently unvaccinated or partially vaccinated, and the link between infections and severe illnesses appears weakened.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: Currently, all of these patients with severe illnesses are either unvaccinated or partially vaccinated.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: For now, it would appear that we have successfully weakened the link between infections and severe illnesses.

sections.label: MTF reopening roadmap packages
sections.summary: The MTF has been developing a roadmap of measures to be implemented step-by-step over the next few months, ensuring each step is safe.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: The MTF has been developing a roadmap comprising packages of measures to be implemented step-by-step over the next few months and with every step, ensuring that opening up is safe for the community.

sections.label: Community care recovery shift
sections.summary: With this change, up to 60% of infected cases are expected to recover in community care facilities instead of acute care hospitals.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: With this change, we expect up to 60% of infected cases to recover in community care facilities instead of in acute care hospitals.

sections.label: Shortened hospital and community stay
sections.summary: Length of stay in hospitals and community care facilities has been shortened, with fully vaccinated persons discharged after 14 days plus a seven-day leave of absence.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: The second change is, we have shortened the length of stay in hospitals and community care facilities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: Previously, most people, generally, were discharged only after 21 days.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: We are now discharging fully vaccinated persons after 14 days from the onset of illness, with a seven-day leave of absence in addition, so long as their tests show that they are COVID-19 negative or have very low viral loads.

sections.label: Home quarantine for vaccinated persons
sections.summary: Fully vaccinated persons can serve quarantine at home if their home is suitable for isolation, with up to 40% expected to do so.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: For fully vaccinated persons, they can now serve their quarantine at home instead of at a dedicated Government facility, provided that their home is suitable for isolation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: We expect that up to 40% of persons under quarantine can serve their quarantine at home and this will go beyond 50% in the coming few weeks as more people get vaccinated.

sections.label: Number not threatening hospital capacity
sections.summary: As of today, despite higher infection cases over the past few days, that number is 14 and does not threaten hospital capacity.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: As of today, despite the higher infection cases over the past few days, that number is 14 and does not threaten our hospital capacity.

sections.label: Reviewing Singapore's COVID-19 vaccine portfolio
sections.summary: Singapore is reviewing its COVID-19 vaccine portfolio and plans to bring in non-mRNA vaccines before the end of the year, subject to supply and regulatory approval.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: We are also continually reviewing Singapore’s portfolio of COVID-19 vaccines.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: We plan to bring in non-mRNA vaccines that are robustly assessed for quality, safety and effectiveness.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: This should happen before the end of the year, subject to supply and regulatory approval.

sections.label: Increasing auto-samplers across sites
sections.summary: Each site can have two or more auto-samplers, and this is being increased to 500 auto-samplers across 400 sites by end of this year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: Every site can have a few, two or more auto-samplers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: We are increasing this to 500 auto-samplers across 400 sites by end of this year.

sections.label: Myocarditis and pericarditis reports received
sections.summary: As of 30 June 2021, HSA had received 12 reports of myocarditis and pericarditis in persons after a dose of the mRNA-based COVID-19 vaccine.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: As of 30 June 2021, HSA had received 12 reports of myocarditis and pericarditis occurring in persons after receiving a dose of the mRNA-based COVID-19 vaccine.

sections.label: Sinovac vaccination doses received
sections.summary: As at 25 July 2021, about 72,000 persons received at least one Sinovac dose and about 17,000 received second doses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: As at 25 July 2021, about 72,000 persons have received at least one dose of the Sinovac vaccine and about 17,000 persons have received their second doses.

sections.label: Sinovac supply and adverse reports
sections.summary: Private clinics can bring in additional Sinovac supply if the Government's 200,000 doses are insufficient, and HSA received 10 adverse event reports as of 9 July 2021.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: If the supply of 200,000 doses which the Government has procured is insufficient to cater to the demand, private clinics can bring in additional supply, as is the case for any other WHO EUL vaccine under the Special Access Route.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: As of 9 July 2021, HSA had received 10 adverse event reports following vaccination with the Sinovac vaccine.

sections.label: Singapore's unique vaccination position
sections.summary: Singapore may be the only country without hospital collapse or high death toll while achieving a very high vaccination rate, due to unity and trust.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: Most of the developing world still has little access to vaccines.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: And even among the countries and regions which have the vaccines, Singapore is unique.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: We have one group, including the US, UK, Israel and many EU countries, which went through major episodes of widespread transmission, hospitals overwhelmed, with many fatalities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: They are now highly vaccinated and opening up their economies and societies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: And then, there is another group, the likes of Australia, New Zealand, Hong Kong, maybe South Korea, who kept the pandemic under control, but are now finding it a challenge to get their people vaccinated, partly because their lives have not been very threatened by COVID-19.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: This will make us perhaps the only country in the world, which has not suffered a collapse of our hospitals nor a high death toll and at the same time, achieved a very high vaccination rate in our population.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: This uniqueness is due to the unity of our people, the trust amongst them and between the people and Government.

sentences.speaker: Mr Deputy Speaker
sentences.text: The Minister for Trade and Industry and the Minister for Finance will be making related Ministerial Statements.

sentences.speaker: Mr Deputy Speaker
sentences.text: I would allow Members to raise points of clarification on all three Statements after the third Statement.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: About a month ago, the MTF Co-Chairs wrote a commentary, outlining a future where Singapore can live normally with COVID-19.

sections.label: Phase Two Heightened Alert questions
sections.summary: The speaker received many questions on whether returning to Phase Two (Heightened Alert) reverses the plan to transition to a COVID-19-endemic state.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: Like Minister Ong, I received many questions on whether our decision to return to Phase Two (Heightened Alert) signals a reversal of our plan to transition to a COVID-19-endemic state.

sections.label: Changi Airport passenger load decline
sections.summary: With Changi Airport's passenger load at only around 3% of pre-COVID-19 levels, demand in these sectors has plummeted.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: With Changi Airport's passenger load at only around 3% of pre-COVID-19 levels – 3%, not 30% – demand in these sectors have plummeted.

sections.label: MTI business support schemes
sections.summary: MTI worked with industry and Government agencies, delivered eight Budgets over one and a half years, and introduced schemes such as the Jobs Support Scheme.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: Since the start of this pandemic, MTI has worked closely with the industry and other Government agencies to help businesses cope.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: We delivered eight Budgets over one and a half years including the Supplementary Supply Bill that we will be debating later, to marshal resources to support businesses and protect jobs.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: We introduced several schemes, such as the Jobs Support Scheme, Jobs Growth Incentive, rental relief and tax rebates.

sections.label: Biomedical and electronics sector growth
sections.summary: Biomedical manufacturing expanded almost 25% last year while electronics grew around 12.5%.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: In particular, the biomedical manufacturing sector expanded significantly by almost 25% last year, while the electronics sector grew around 12.5%.

sections.label: Easing social restrictions and business demand
sections.summary: Social restrictions will ease, with vaccinated people having wider access and unvaccinated needing a negative Pre-Event Test.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: For example, restrictions on social gatherings will ease and we can expect larger dining-in group sizes and lower requirements and higher capacity for various events.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: We will take a differentiated approach: vaccinated individuals will be able to engage in a wider range of social activities and in larger groups, while those who are unvaccinated will only be able to do so with a negative Pre-Event Test (PET) result.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: With this, F&B, retail and other businesses that provide in-person services, such as gyms and beauty services, will see a return in demand.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: Sectors, such as tourism, cruise and MICE will also get some relief as capacity limits are progressively raised, although foreign tourists will still take some time to return.

sections.label: Flexible work and border relaxation
sections.summary: Flexible work arrangements and business continuity plans continue, and border restrictions are being looked at for relaxation.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: And third, continue allowing flexible work arrangements and putting in place business continuity plans to strengthen operational resilience.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: We are also looking at relaxing our border restrictions safely.

sections.label: Vaccination, travel and endemic state
sections.summary: With higher vaccination coverage, travel will be facilitated and restrictions eventually lifted, though some measures may remain.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: This has not been easy for many of them.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: Therefore, as our vaccination coverage increases and the majority of residents here are protected against COVID-19, we will also progressively facilitate international travel with countries that have managed COVID-19 well and allow fully vaccinated persons to travel and to do business more freely.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: We are working this out carefully and engaging our partner countries and will provide more details when ready.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: We will continue to push for higher vaccination coverage and if the incidence of severe illness from COVID-19 remains low despite clusters emerging from time to time, we will eventually be able to arrive at a truly endemic state.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: Practically all social and workplace restrictions can be lifted, although some critical measures, such as mask-wearing and precautions for large events may remain.

sections.label: Investment commitments and major companies
sections.summary: Investors committed S$17.2 billion in 2020, and investments came from biomedical and electronics companies including Sanofi, BioNTech and GlobalFoundries.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: Despite the challenging environment, investors committed S$17.2 billion in investment in 2020, the highest in 12 years.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: More recently, we also attracted significant investments from major biomedical and electronics companies, such as Sanofi in April, BioNTech in May and GlobalFoundries in June.

sections.label: Heightened Alert and unvaccinated seniors
sections.summary: Over 200,000 seniors aged 60 and above are not fully vaccinated, so the MTF scaled back activities to Phase Two (Heightened Alert).

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: This was when we moved into Heightened Alert.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: And we are especially worried about our seniors because there are still over 200,000 seniors aged 60 and above who are not fully vaccinated.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: If they catch the virus, many would likely become severely ill or even succumb to the infection.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: That is why, as you heard just now from my Co-Chairs just now, the MTF made the difficult decision to scale back activities and return to Phase Two (Heightened Alert).

sections.label: Support package for workers and businesses
sections.summary: MOF announced a new $1.1 billion support package last Friday to cushion the impact on workers and businesses.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: We also know these measures will be difficult for our workers and businesses.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: This is why MOF announced a new $1.1 billion support package last Friday to cushion the impact.

sections.label: Easing measures for vaccinated persons
sections.summary: If clusters are controlled and hospitalisation rates stay low, some Phase Two (Heightened Alert) measures will be eased only for vaccinated persons.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Importantly, by then, two-thirds of our population would have received two doses and we would have vaccinated about three-quarters of our seniors aged 70 and above.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: So, if the clusters are under control and hospitalisation rates remain low, we will be able to ease some of the Phase Two (Heightened Alert) measures.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: But the easing will be differentiated and extended to only vaccinated persons because they are much better protected against the effects of the virus.

sections.label: Vaccination targets by early September
sections.summary: By around early September, about 80% of the population is expected to receive two doses, with similar coverage hoped for seniors aged 70 and above.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: By around early September, we expect to vaccinate about 80% of our population with two doses and we hope to cover a similar proportion of our seniors aged 70 and above.

sections.label: Travel and Stay-Home Notice rules
sections.summary: Fully vaccinated persons can travel to these countries or region without the full 14-day hotel Stay-Home Notice, replaced by testing or a seven-day home notice.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Fully vaccinated persons will then be able to travel to these countries or region without needing to serve the full 14-day Stay-Home Notice (SHN) in a hotel when they return.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Depending on the risk level of the country they visit, we will either replace the SHN with a rigorous testing regime or shorten the SHN to seven days at home.

sections.label: Readiness to slow down reopening
sections.summary: These measures must remain acceptable and stable before proceeding, but a rise in hospitalisation or severe illness may require slowing down or pulling back.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: We will ensure that these remain acceptable and stable before we proceed to the next step.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: But if hospitalisation cases, or worse, severe illnesses were to shoot up, we will have to be prepared to slow down, or even pull back.

sections.label: Vaccination key to reopening plans
sections.summary: With better vaccination coverage, plans to reopen progressively can resume while keeping everyone safe, with vaccination for seniors underlined as key.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: With better vaccination coverage, we will soon be able to resume our plans to reopen progressively, while keeping everyone safe.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: But I underline: vaccination is key, especially vaccination for our seniors.

sections.label: Stay home if unwell
sections.summary: People who are not feeling well should stay home.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: If you are not feeling well, stay home.

sections.label: SMS alert testing response
sections.summary: Those receiving an SMS alert should be tested soon and limit social interactions until a negative result, as testing is now more affordable, accessible and convenient.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: If you receive an SMS alert, come forward to be tested as soon as possible and minimise your social interactions until you have a confirmed negative test result.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: There is no excuse not to be tested, since testing is now more affordable, accessible and convenient than it used to be and will continue to be so in the future.

sections.label: Test kit distribution and new testing
sections.summary: The MTF is distributing test kits to households, starting near markets with large clusters and scaling up to everyone, and rolling out wastewater surveillance and breathalyser tests.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: The MTF is also distributing these test kits to households.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: We are starting with those who live near markets where large clusters have been identified and we will progressively scale up and distribute to everyone in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: As you heard just now, we are also rolling out new methods of testing, be it wastewater surveillance in our estates, or breathalyser tests at our checkpoints.

sections.label: Questions on KTVs and nightclubs
sections.summary: Questions have been raised about why KTVs and nightclubs operated as F&B outlets, enforcement, hostesses, and their immigration status.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: In this House and outside, there have been a number of questions related to KTVs: why were KTVs and nightclubs allowed to operate as F&B outlets; the enforcement regime in respect to these outlets; why were hostesses allowed in those places; and the immigration status of these providing hostessing service at these places.

sections.label: Local workers employed end 2019
sections.summary: The assessment is that they probably employed about 10,000 local workers as of end 2019.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: Our assessment is that they probably employ about 10,000 local workers as of end 2019.

sections.label: KTV operations remain forbidden
sections.summary: A pilot project for KTVs with strict conditions was considered but not proceeded with, and KTV operations remain forbidden from March 2020 until now.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: At one time, we considered possibly allowing a pilot project for KTVs with very strict conditions but eventually we did not proceed.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: So, the first point to note is that from March 2020 until now, KTV operations remain forbidden.

sections.label: Nightlife businesses converted or exited
sections.summary: More than 400 such businesses converted and about 100 exited the nightlife industry, while MTF and the Government knew some KTV operations, pubs and bars had dodgy reputations.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: More than 400 such businesses converted and about 100 exited the nightlife industry.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: At the same time, we were considering this, that yes, MTF and the Government do know that there are some KTV operations, pubs and bars with dodgy reputations.

sections.label: KTV cluster under control
sections.summary: The KTV cluster was brought under control fairly quickly through tracing, testing and ringfencing, with about five new linked cases daily and 232 cases as of 24 July.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: As he has said in his speech, the KTV cluster has been brought under control fairly quickly: tracing, testing, ringfencing the cases.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: So, we have about five new cases linked to the KTV cluster each day for the past few days.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: I have the figures as of 24 July: 232 cases, 49 in the hospital, none have been in or are in the ICU.

sections.label: Tightening due to Jurong Fishery Port
sections.summary: The tightening of the measures was due to the cluster at the Jurong Fishery Port.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: The tightening of the measures was due to the cluster at the Jurong Fishery Port (JFP).

sections.label: Police operations against pivoted outlets
sections.summary: From October 2020 to 10 July 2021, the Police conducted 202 operations against pivoted outlets and other outlets operating illegally.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: During the period October 2020 to 10 July 2021, the Police conducted 202 operations against pivoted outlets as well as other outlets which were operating illegally.

sections.label: Enforcement results from daily operations
sections.summary: One operation every day resulted in detection of 58 Public Entertainment Act and Liquor Control Act infringements, 595 SMM breaches and 142 arrests under various laws.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: This, I think, should put to rest any questions about enforcement actions by the Police; one operation every day.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: That has resulted in the detection of 58 Public Entertainment Act, Liquor Control Act infringements, 595 SMM breaches, 142 arrests for offences under various laws including the Public Entertainment Act, Liquor Control Act, Employment of Foreign Manpower Act, Immigration Act; not all in pivoted places but also completely illegal operations.

sections.label: Closure orders on F&B outlets
sections.summary: Agencies imposed around 100 closure orders on F&B outlets including about 40 pivoted outlets, and SFA revoked the food licence of seven pivoted outlets as of 23 July.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: To date, agencies have imposed around 100 closure orders on F&B outlets including on about 40 pivoted outlets.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: As I said to the House just now, there were about 437 pivoted outlets, so roughly 10% have been acting illegally and about 60 other F&B outlets also were in breach.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: So, SFA has revoked the food licence of seven pivoted outlets as of 23 July.

sections.label: Woman entered under Familial Ties Lane
sections.summary: A woman linked to the KTV cluster entered Singapore in February 2021 under the Familial Ties Lane, sponsored by a Singapore Citizen who applied as her boyfriend.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: The first woman linked to the KTV cluster, much attention has centred on her, had come into Singapore in February 2021, through the "boyfriend/girlfriend" category, under what we call the Familial Ties Lane and I will refer to it as FTL, sponsored by a Singapore Citizen who applied for her on the basis that he was her boyfriend.

sections.label: Girlfriend/boyfriend category removed
sections.summary: In March 2021, the girlfriend/boyfriend category for entry applications was removed.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: But when we looked at these applications for girlfriends and they are all primarily girlfriends, to come in, we decided this would not do, we have to stop this.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: So, in March 2021, this "girlfriend/boyfriend" category was removed.

sections.label: ICA action on dodgy applications
sections.summary: ICA rescinded approvals, barred entry and suspended sponsors and travellers from future applications for dodgy applications, and other entry avenues are very limited.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: ICA has also taken action in respect of dodgy applications by rescinding the approvals, barring the travellers from entry into Singapore and suspending the sponsors and travellers from future applications.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: Apart from the FTL category, we have other avenues for foreigners to enter into Singapore during this pandemic but very limited.

sections.label: 29 women arrested in nightlife operations
sections.summary: 29 women aged 20 to 47 of various nationalities were arrested for offences under the Employment of Foreign Manpower Act and other laws, including various pass holders.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: Tying that back to the Police's recent operations against nightlife outlets, 29 women, aged between 20 and 47, of various nationalities, have been arrested for offences under the Employment of Foreign Manpower Act and other laws.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: The 29 include Permanent Residents, Work Pass holders, S Pass holders, Short-Term Pass holder; one who came in under the Unilateral Opening, five who had come in under the "girlfriend" category; Long-Term Visit Pass holders, other passes, Student Pass, Dependant's Pass.

sections.label: Passes cancelled and deportations
sections.summary: TraceTogether data cannot be used, and 16 women have had their passes cancelled and have been or will be deported, with investigations ongoing for the others.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: And as Members will know, we cannot use the TraceTogether data for this.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: So far, 16 women have had their passes cancelled and they have been or will be deported.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: Investigations are ongoing in respect of the other women.

sections.label: Enforcement numbers from October to July
sections.summary: The Minister mentioned 202 enforcements from October last year to July this year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The Minister mentioned a few numbers – 202 enforcements from October last year to July this year.

sections.label: KTV establishment licence revocations
sections.summary: The Minister said seven establishments had licences revoked, and asks whether the 10% in breach, about 40 establishments, will also be revoked.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The Minister spoke of, I think, a total of seven establishments – and I stand corrected if I am wrong – seven establishments that have seen their licences revoked but about 10% of the pivoted KTV establishments have been in breach of regulations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Are the licences for that 10% – which I think will extend to 40 establishments – going to be revoked as well?

sections.label: Vaccination rate and reopening economy
sections.summary: Reaching an 80% vaccination rate around September or October will allow a bigger reopening, but not a big bang reopening, while severe cases are monitored.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: As soon as we are able to reach our vaccination rate of 80% and above around September or October, we will be able to move in a bigger way to reopen the economy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: But I also want to point out that we are not likely to have a big bang reopening because it is important for us, as Minister Ong and I have mentioned earlier, to continue to monitor the number of severe cases.

sections.label: Enforcement regime intensity
sections.summary: Mr Singh asked if the enforcement regime is heightened, and it can be assumed one enforcement action per day is intense, from October last year to July this year.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: First, on the enforcement regime, I think Mr Singh wanted to know if it is heightened.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: We can assume that if there was one enforcement action per day, it is quite intense and it has been so from October of last year to July of this year, right from the beginning.

sections.label: Closed establishments and breach numbers
sections.summary: Mr Singh wanted to know about the seven closed establishments, but 10% were in breach, about 40-odd out of the 400 which had pivoted.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Third, I think Mr Singh wanted to know – seven have been closed, but I pointed out that 10% were in breach, about 40-odd out of the 400 which had pivoted.

sections.label: Penalty and breach point system
sections.summary: The penalty is transparent and imposed according to the kind of breach, and there is a point system for breaches which lead to closure.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: The penalty is transparent and the penalty will be imposed according to the kind of breach that has been committed.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: And I think most people will know that there is also a point system for breaches which lead to closure.

sections.label: Vaccine supply and senior vaccination
sections.summary: Some deliveries were brought forward and confirmed, so there has been no supply problem for the past month or two; the constraint is more people, especially seniors, getting vaccinated.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: And, lately, we were able to bring forward and confirm some of the deliveries.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: So, as of now, for the past month or two, we have not had a supply problem.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: Our constraint now is we need more people, especially our seniors, to come forward and get vaccinated.

sections.label: Vaccination differentiation public health reasons
sections.summary: The speaker says it is not discrimination because there are good public health reasons to differentiate treatment between vaccinated and unvaccinated people.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: I will provide some answers, then I will invite Minister Grace Fu to supplement with her clarifications.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: I would not call it discrimination because there are good public health reasons to differentiate the treatment between those who are vaccinated and not vaccinated.

sections.label: Vaccination status record
sections.summary: The speaker says theirs states that they are vaccinated.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: Mine does; it says that I am vaccinated.

sections.label: Mid-term review and pre-event testing
sections.summary: The mid-term review will take into account these provisions, and those who cannot be vaccinated may take a Pre-event Test to join such a group.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: So, I think, when we do our mid-term review, we will also take into account these provisions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: And as for those who cannot be vaccinated or unvaccinated for some reason, but want to join such a group, we had earlier also allowed them to take a PET (Pre-event Test).

sections.label: High vaccination rate reduces differentiation
sections.summary: At a very high vaccination rate there should be very little differentiation between vaccinated and unvaccinated because collectively we will be very resilient.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: When we get to a very high level of vaccination rate, there should be very little differentiation between vaccinated and unvaccinated, because collectively, we will be very resilient.

sections.label: Phylogenetic study multiple entry points
sections.summary: Phylogenetic study shows there are likely multiple points of entry because of slight genetic differences in the virus and infections across the cluster.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: As I mentioned earlier, phylogenetic study shows that there is likely to be multiple points of entry because there are slight genetic differences in the virus and the infections across the cluster.

sections.label: Seafood imports at Jurong and Senoko
sections.summary: JFP handles about 30% of total seafood imports and is complemented by Senoko Fishery Port, which handles about 4%.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: JFP handles about 30% of our total seafood imports and is complemented by Senoko Fishery Port (SFP), which handles about 4% of seafood imports.

sections.label: Seafood supply stability
sections.summary: Seafood supply stayed stable despite JFP's closure and local market disruptions.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: Our seafood supply has remained stable, despite the closure of JFP and local disruptions at our markets.

sections.label: JFP worker vaccination rates
sections.summary: 76% of JFP workers are fully vaccinated and 86% received at least one dose.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: To date, 76% of workers at JFP are fully vaccinated, while 86% have received at least one dose of vaccine.

sections.label: JFP closure and quarantine orders
sections.summary: MOH closed JFP from 17 to 31 July, issued Quarantine Orders to all 684 workers, and identified areas for improvement.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: In order to break the chains of transmission, MOH made a difficult, but necessary decision to close JFP for two weeks from 17 to 31 July with all 684 workers issued Quarantine Orders.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: We are not waiting for the investigations to complete because as Minister Ong has mentioned, it is important for us to act immediately to protect public health.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: So, on our own, our preliminary review has identified some areas for improvement.

sections.label: Rostered Routine Testing at JFP
sections.summary: SFA will work with companies on seven-day Rostered Routine Testing for all JFP workers, who are encouraged to get vaccinated.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: SFA will work with companies to implement seven-day Rostered Routine Testing (RRT) for all workers at JFP and all workers will be encouraged to get vaccinated.

sections.label: Rental waiver for qualifying tenants
sections.summary: Government will provide an additional four-week rental waiver for qualifying tenants on Government-owned commercial properties.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: As announced by MOF last week, the Government will provide an additional four-week rental waiver for qualifying tenants on Government-owned commercial properties.

sections.label: Market and hawker relief fund
sections.summary: A one-off $500 cash assistance will be disbursed in August to each cooked food and market stallholder in NEA-managed centres.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: A one-off cash assistance of $500 under the Market and Hawker Centre Relief Fund will be disbursed to each stallholder of cooked food and market stalls in centres managed by NEA or NEA-appointed operators in August.

sections.label: Rostered testing for stallholders
sections.summary: Stallholders will undergo Rostered Routine Testing every 14 days as an extra precaution to protect their health and safety.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: So, we are taking extra precaution to make sure that their health and safety are protected.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: We will carry out Rostered Routine Testing for stallholders once every 14 days.

sections.label: Market and hawker centre vaccination
sections.summary: About 90% of those working in markets and hawker centres, including stallholders, hawkers and cleaners, have received at least one vaccine dose.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: About 90% of those working in markets and hawker centres – these include our stallholders, our hawkers as well as our cleaners at the centres – have received at least one dose of the vaccine.

sections.label: Patrons returning used trays
sections.summary: When dine-in resumes, patrons are reminded to return their own used trays, crockery and litter to help create a cleaner dining environment.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: When dine-in resumes, patrons are reminded that they can do their part by returning their own used trays, crockery and litter to help create a cleaner dining environment.

sections.label: Identifying higher-risk workplaces
sections.summary: The passage asks what measures can be taken to better identify workplaces that may have a higher risk of transmission compared to elsewhere.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: What measures can we take to better identify workplaces that may have a higher risk of transmission compared to elsewhere?

sections.label: No school-based transmission yet
sections.summary: In recent outbreaks there has been no school-based transmission; infected students caught the virus at home from family members.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: Up to now, in the recent outbreaks, we have not had school-based transmission.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: We have had students who have been infected from their home, from family members, but not yet school-based transmission.

sections.label: Vaccination waiting and Sinovac seniors
sections.summary: 72,000 people have gotten their doses, and only 10% of Sinovac recipients are Singaporean seniors above 60.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: It may involve some waiting, but they will eventually get their vaccinations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: I have reported just now that 72,000 people have gotten their doses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: For all those who have taken the Sinovac vaccine, only 10% are Singaporean seniors above 60 years old.

sections.label: two-five rule and seniors
sections.summary: The two-five rule was prepared to proceed until significant community transmissions and low senior vaccination rates were found.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: When we introduced the "two-five rule" we were prepared to go ahead with it, until we found that there was a significant number of transmissions within the community and the vaccination rate of our seniors was still relatively low.

sections.label: weighing two-five rule risks
sections.summary: It was important to weigh proceeding with the two-five rule against reversing it to allow vaccination rates to improve.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: Of course, one option was to proceed with it, come hell or high water.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: But the risk was that you may see a significant number of seniors being infected and because they would still be unvaccinated, they would still be at risk of severe outcome and even mortality.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: You may think that, well, that is okay, then just do not allow the unvaccinated to go to the restaurants.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: But you must also remember that those who go to the restaurants and are vaccinated may still be infected and bring the virus back home to the families where there are seniors who are unvaccinated.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: Therefore, it was important for us to weigh the pros and cons between proceeding with the two-five rule, or to make a painful decision to reverse the decision and give ourselves more time to allow the vaccination rate to improve, both the general vaccination rate as well as the seniors' vaccination rate.

sections.label: mask-off eating and drinking
sections.summary: The most critical difference is that activities are mask-off as customers remove masks to eat and drink.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: The most critical difference is that their activities are mask-off, as customers have to remove their masks when they eat and drink.

sections.label: strengthening border SMMs
sections.summary: They are looking at how to strengthen SMMs at the border and started contactless delivery since April.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: We are looking at how to strengthen the SMMs at the border.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: We have already started contactless delivery since April.

sections.label: contactless crewmen fish transfer
sections.summary: Crewmen are contactless, not allowed to land, staying on the vessel and using vessel equipment to move fish to shore.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: The crewmen right now, they are actually contactless, in other words, they are not allowed to land, they will stay on the vessel and they will use the vessel equipment to move their buckets of fish onto the shore and our shore workers will take over.

sections.label: Sinovac reflected in Health Hub
sections.summary: Vaccination with Sinovac now reflects in the Health Hub app with the letters SAR.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: Actually, if one is vaccinated with Sinovac now, it does reflect in your Health Hub app and in brackets the letters "SAR".

sections.label: Sinovac PSAR data incomplete
sections.summary: Sinovac's earlier PSAR application to HSA was made when the data was not yet complete.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: At the same time, when Sinovac applied to HSA for Pandemic Special Access Route (PSAR) approval earlier, the data was not yet complete.

sections.label: Opening up for vaccinated travellers
sections.summary: Regions with similar infection control and risk levels could open to vaccinated travellers without Stay-Home Notices but with tests.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: The next step is for those regions that have also controlled their infections and have a risk level about the same as ours – we can, for example, open up for vaccinated travellers, to and fro, without the need for Stay-Home Notices (SHNs) but require a series of tests.

sections.label: Compulsory vaccination not yet time
sections.summary: It is not yet time to consider whether vaccination can be made compulsory like MMR and others.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: Whether we can make vaccination compulsory like we did for measles, mumps and rubella (MMR) and others, it is not time yet to think about that proposition.

sections.label: SafeEntry check-in across all markets
sections.summary: SafeEntry check-in was done only for popular markets, but is now planned across all markets and hawker centres.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: So, we only did it for the very popular markets.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: But now, we are planning, based on the lessons we have learned and realising how effective it is, we are planning to put in SafeEntry check-in requirements across all markets and hawker centres.

sections.label: Quick Test Centres as infrastructure
sections.summary: Quick Test Centres may become almost national infrastructure, with employers possibly requiring employee testing every 14 or seven days.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: I have a supplementary question on the Quick Test Centres.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: I think the quick test centres, in time to come, are likely to be almost a national infrastructure for living with endemic COVID-19.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: I can imagine buildings and employers requiring that their employees should be tested once every 14 days or seven days before coming to work as a precaution, as part of living with COVID-19.

sections.label: Five days, 10am to 5pm
sections.summary: The current arrangement is five days, 10.00 am to 5.00 pm, because many F&B outlets find weekends unsuitable.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: Right now, it is five days, 10.00 am to 5.00 pm, I think, because many of the F&B outlets find that weekends are not suitable for them.

sections.label: Vaccination coverage and National Day
sections.summary: First-dose uptake is 76% overall and 85-88% by age band except those above 70 at 76%, with two doses possibly near 70% by National Day and 80% by September.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: Right now, those who have taken the first jab, it is already 76% and that is over the whole population, including those under 12.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: And if you break it down by age bands, it is well over 80% – 85% to 88% – except for the most senior group, age above 70, which is at 76%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: So, just based on who has taken the first dose and so long as they turn up for second doses which they tend to, by the time we reach National Day, we should be close to 70% receiving two doses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: And we believe that if that momentum continues, by September, I think there is a very good possibility that we will reach 80%.

sections.label: Sinovac data submission
sections.summary: As of 5 July, Sinovac submitted all required data for evaluation under the PSAR framework.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: As of 5 July, Sinovac has submitted all the required data for us to do a proper evaluation under our PSAR framework.

sections.label: Purchase agreements and donations
sections.summary: Strict contractual requirements in purchase agreements prevent taking delivery and donating vaccines to another country or region.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: As for helping our immediate neighbours, all these purchase agreements have quite strict contractual requirements.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: So, we cannot take delivery and then donate to another country or region.

sections.label: Reopening moves amid uncertainty
sections.summary: The fluid and uncertain situation makes it hard, so one move comes in early August, mid-term of Phase Two (Heightened Alert), and another at about 80% coverage.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: Unfortunately, with the current situation being so fluid and uncertain, it is very hard.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: That is why, beyond, I said early August, mid-term of the Phase Two (Heightened Alert), we have one move.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: When we get to about 80% coverage, we make another move.

sections.label: Spikes and reopening pullback
sections.summary: If cases spike, the next reopening step may be slowed or, in the worst case, pulled back if many unvaccinated and elderly fall sick in hospitals.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: If these were to spike, then as I have said, we might either have to slow down on the next step of reopening or, in the very worst case, if indeed, a lot of unvaccinated persons and a lot of elderly turn up sick in the hospitals, then we may really have to pull back, as I have mentioned.

sections.label: Third dose booster study
sections.summary: The US and Singapore have not concluded, and are actively studying whether a third dose booster is needed, when, and what strategy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: If I am not wrong, the US has not come to a conclusion and neither have we.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: We are studying this actively whether we need a third dose as a booster, when and what kind of strategy – whether you use back mRNA or use a heterologous strategy.

sections.label: Vice activities going underground
sections.summary: The member asks whether vice activities may be driven underground to other settings and how surveillance and enforcement will be stepped up.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: I just have a follow-up question which is: given that there were rules to disallow hostessing and yet there was blatant disregard for the rules and now, with the spotlight on these KTVs or pivoted outlets, I am just wondering whether there is a risk that more of these vice activities may then be driven underground to other settings.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: Therefore, how will the surveillance and enforcement be stepped up to control this?

sections.label: Prostitution not illegal in Singapore
sections.summary: Prostitution was and is not illegal in Singapore, and banning it would have caused job losses and driven it underground.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Singapore never made prostitution illegal because we knew that countries which had tried and for thousands of years people have tried, it is not going to work.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Prostitution was neither illegal then nor is it now, except, I suppose, when there are safe distancing measures.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Supposing we had said no to all of them, there would have been a great deal of loss of jobs.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Precisely, this issue, it would have gone underground much more and it would have been very difficult to trace.

sections.label: Heavy onus on regulatory authorities
sections.summary: The passage states a heavy onus falls on regulatory authorities, citing girlfriends with Singapore sponsors after a unilateral opening closed.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: It puts a heavy onus on the regulatory authorities.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: But as you saw from the example I gave, immediately after the unilateral opening was closed, there were many girlfriends standing up with Singapore sponsors with a variety of reasons and this will go on.
